“Labour is divided into three formal stages. The first stage begins with established labour and ends when the cervix is fully dilated at 10 cm. It includes cervical effacement and progressive dilatation with descent and rotation of the fetal presenting part. The second stage begins at full dilatation and ends with birth of the baby. It can be divided into passive and active phases, with descent and maternal expulsive efforts occurring in the active phase. The third stage begins after birth of the baby and ends with delivery of the placenta and membranes. Throughout all three stages I would continuously assess maternal wellbeing, fetal wellbeing and progress of labour, while providing appropriate analgesia, support and timely intervention if abnormalities develop.”
